choices.content: \(a\) to the power of \(n\) plus \(b\) to the power of \(n\)
Only the 2 terms \(a\) to the power of \(n\) and \(b\) to the power of \(n\)
\(C(n,k)\) multiplied by \(a\) to the power of \(n-k\), then multiplied by \(b\) to the power of \(k\)

question.prompt: What is the general term in the expansion of \((a+b)^n\) using the binomial theorem?

solutions.explanation: Each term includes a combination number, and the exponents of \(a\) and \(b\) add up to \(n\).
solutions.title: Recognize the general-term structure
